baseline.svg.title: E1: 1000-path baseline acquisition
baseline.svg.explanation: a=b=1, Delta=.5, alpha=.15, T=50, dt=.001; original initial phase asin(.5)+.5. Representative paths are first five recorded streams.
baseline.svg.interpretation: The ensemble mean describes acquisition; the CI quantifies uncertainty in that mean. Individual paths fluctuate more widely.
baseline.svg.limitations: Pointwise CIs are not simultaneous bands and do not enclose 95% of trajectories. The stationary formula is local and assumes no slips.

noise_detuning.svg.title: E2-E3: noise and detuning sensitivity
noise_detuning.svg.explanation: Plots are slices of the full grid, not additional independent simulations. Error bars use trajectory bootstrap variance intervals or t/Wilson intervals as appropriate.
noise_detuning.svg.interpretation: Increasing noise broadens the phase distribution. Detuning approaches the local saddle-node and changes capture and transport.
noise_detuning.svg.limitations: Terminal capture is an operational finite-time criterion. Above-threshold cells have no locking or phase-slip probability.

combined_grid.svg.title: E4: complete 72-condition grid
combined_grid.svg.explanation: All eight noise values and nine detunings were executed. Missing locking/slip cells above threshold are deliberately masked.
combined_grid.svg.interpretation: Variance, phase transport and committed transitions describe distinct outcomes; no single metric defines global lock.
combined_grid.svg.limitations: T=50 is finite. Deterministic alpha=0 controls have one path; stochastic cells have 500 or 1000 independent paths.

slip_survival.svg.title: E6: censoring and detector sensitivity
slip_survival.svg.explanation: Six 1000-path ensembles run to T=200. Kaplan-Meier curves retain all right-censored trajectories; no event is represented by censoring, not a fictitious zero waiting time.
slip_survival.svg.interpretation: Longer runs resolve selected near-threshold escapes. Differences between detectors quantify sensitivity to commitment definitions.
slip_survival.svg.limitations: Zero observed events do not establish a zero true rate. A bootstrap interval is degenerate at zero when every path has zero events; use the separately reported probability upper bounds.

slip_geometry.svg.title: E6: well transitions and saddle geometry
slip_geometry.svg.explanation: Left: recorded condition delta=.99, alpha=.4 with primary committed-slip events. Right: backward integration along the stable eigenvector of the saddle at delta=.5, epsilon=1e-6.
slip_geometry.svg.interpretation: The true deterministic basin separator is two-dimensional; a phase-only boundary cannot encode velocity-dependent capture.
slip_geometry.svg.limitations: The manifold is a local numerical approximation. The detector uses persistent well cores, not an exact stochastic separatrix. Commitment times lag barrier crossings.

potential_barrier.svg.title: Mathematical mechanism: shrinking escape barrier
potential_barrier.svg.explanation: Derived from U(phi)=-Delta*phi-ab*cos(phi), a=b=1. This is an analytical diagram, not an estimated escape-rate curve.
potential_barrier.svg.interpretation: The downhill barrier tends to zero as delta approaches one, providing a mechanistic explanation for increased escape susceptibility.
potential_barrier.svg.limitations: Barrier height alone does not give a finite-noise inertial escape rate, global capture range, or proof of asymptotic stochastic stability.

convergence.svg.title: E5: coupled numerical refinement
convergence.svg.explanation: 1000 baseline and 500 near-threshold Brownian paths, T=10. Reference dt=.00015625; all coarser increments are sums of the same fine increments. Strong intervals bootstrap paired path errors.
convergence.svg.interpretation: Observed fitted slopes describe finite-step error relative to this reference. Paired weak intervals expose sampling uncertainty in mean differences.
convergence.svg.limitations: The reference is numerical; slopes are empirical and partly affected by reference error. No improved Milstein method is claimed. T=10 convergence does not prove T=200 rare-event count accuracy.

parameter_sensitivity.svg.title: E7: varying a, b and noise at fixed Delta=.5
parameter_sensitivity.svg.explanation: 18 conditions, 500 independent paths per condition, T=50, dt=.001. The raw table also reports variance, capture, events and first-passage outcomes.
parameter_sensitivity.svg.interpretation: Changing a and b changes normalized detuning, damping and noise response simultaneously; combinations below the equilibrium threshold exhibit phase transport.
parameter_sensitivity.svg.limitations: This fixed-Delta design measures joint physical changes, not a standardized one-at-a-time causal derivative. Finite rotation is not numerical divergence.

brownian.svg.title: Brownian increments and variance scaling
brownian.svg.explanation: A reproducible generated example (seed 20261113), separate from the experiment cohorts. Independent Gaussian increments have variance dt.
brownian.svg.interpretation: Multiplying standard-normal samples by sqrt(dt) produces the correct Wiener increment scale.
brownian.svg.limitations: One path is an illustration; the 200,000-increment automated preflight supplies the variance check.

synthetic_synchronization.svg: Tail mean Kuramoto order parameter over t=40 to 50 for 500 independent network trajectories per cell. Error bars are Student-t 95% CIs across network aggregates. Communication has no delay or dropout. Higher rho reduces differential noise at fixed marginal intensity; rho=1 shared additive noise cancels from relative dynamics. The N=3 ring and complete graphs are identical and do not constitute independent topology evidence.
synthetic_impairments.svg: Sparse fixed graphs: tail mean pairwise phase disagreement, averaged over unordered pairs as 1-cos(theta_j-theta_i), across 500 independent networks per cell. Error bars are Student-t 95% CIs. Dropout probability is .3 when enabled and stale relative-error delay is .2 when enabled. Original degree normalization means dropout also reduces expected coupling strength; this comparison does not isolate random interruption at fixed effective coupling.
synthetic_timeseries.svg: Ensemble mean Kuramoto order parameter for ring networks with dropout=.3 and relative-error delay=.2. Shading is a pointwise Student-t 95% confidence interval for the mean of 500 independent networks, not a path containment or simultaneous band. Each trajectory has random initial phases and independent noise streams; the three rho conditions reuse matched underlying streams. The common additive component rotates the network globally without changing relative phases in this specified delayed-relative-error model.
synthetic_factorial.svg: Complete 144-cell synthetic factorial matrix. Entries are mean tail order parameter R over t=40 to 50, estimated from 500 independent network trajectories per cell. Every topology, network size, noise correlation and communication impairment appears. Detailed 95% network-level confidence intervals are in synthetic_summary.csv; this heatmap shows means only. Matched conditions reuse network inputs. For N=3, complete and ring are the same graph. A single fixed frequency vector and sparse graph are used per network size, so these results do not average over graph/frequency populations.
synthetic_ring_states.svg: Two selected executed N8 ring networks at rho=1 with clean communication. At rho=1 the relative dynamics are deterministic, so noiseless replays recover each original tail R exactly (absolute error0). Replicate0 has tailR=.98962 and winding0; replicate6 has tailR=.07925 and winding-1, despite tail frequency dispersion2.83e-7 radians/model time. Accumulating principal wrapped neighbor gaps around the ring exposes this twisted phase configuration. These are diagnostic replays of existing rows, not extra independent network replications or a classification of all500 rows.
